title: The Prophet (may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him) did not offer a prayer after the revelation of {When there comes Allah’s help and the conquest} [Surat an-Nasr: 1] except that he would say therein: "Subhānaka Rabbana wa bihamdik, Allāhumma ighfir li (Glory and praise be to You, our Lord. O Allah, forgive me)
hadeeth: ‘Ā’ishah, Mother of the Believers, (may Allah be pleased with her) reported: The Prophet (may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him) did not offer a prayer after the revelation of {When there comes Allah’s help and the conquest} [Surat an-Nasr: 1] except that he would say therein: "Subhānaka Rabbana wa bihamdik, Allāhumma ighfir li (Glory and praise be to You, our Lord. O Allah, forgive me)". She also reported: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him) used to say frequently in his Rukū‘ and Sujūd: "Subhānak Allāhumma Rabbana wa bihamdik, Allāhumma ighfir li (Glory and praise be to You, O Allah, our Lord. O Allah, forgive me)" in compliance with the command in the Qur’an.
explanation: ‘Ā’ishah, Mother of the Believers (may Allah be pleased with her), informs that upon the revelation of {When there comes Allah’s help and the conquest} to the Prophet (may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him), he complied with the command in the Qur’an and hastened to obey the command of Allah Almighty in His saying: {Then glorify the praise of your Lord, and ask His forgiveness}. Therefore, he used to frequently say in his Rukū‘ (bowing) and Sujūd (prostration) during the prayer, "Glory be to You," and may You be Exalted above any deficiency that does not befit You. "And praise, O Allah, our Lord," praise that is rightfully due to You for the perfection of Your essence, attributes, and actions. "O Allah, forgive me" and erase and overlook my sin.
hints: It is recommended to say this supplication frequently in Rukū‘ and Sujūd.

Seeking forgiveness at the end of one’s life serves as a reminder to conclude acts of worship—especially the prayer—with seeking forgiveness to make up for any shortcomings that might have occurred in them.
The best thing to use in imploring Allah for accepting supplications is mentioning His praises, exalting Him, and declaring Him free from imperfections and flaws.
The merit of seeking Allah's forgiveness and pursuing it in all conditions.
The perfect servitude of the Prophet (may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him) and his compliance with the command of Allah.
hadeeth_intro: ‘Ā’ishah, Mother of the Believers, (may Allah be pleased with her) reported:
hadeeth_ar:
عَنْ عَائِشَةَ أُمِّ المُؤْمِنينَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا قَالَتْ: مَا صَلَّى النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ صَلاَةً بَعْدَ أَنْ نَزَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ: {إِذَا جَاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ وَالفَتْحُ} [النصر: 1] إِلَّا يَقُولُ فِيهَا: «سُبْحَانَكَ رَبَّنَا وَبِحَمْدِكَ اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي».
وعَنْها قَالَتْ: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يُكْثِرُ أَنْ يَقُولَ فِي رُكُوعِهِ وَسُجُودِهِ: «سُبْحَانَكَ اللهُمَّ رَبَّنَا وَبِحَمْدِكَ، اللهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي» يَتَأَوَّلُ الْقُرْآنَ.
hadeeth_intro_ar: عَنْ عَائِشَةَ أُمِّ المُؤْمِنينَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا قَالَتْ:
explanation_ar: تُخْبِرُ أمُّ المؤمنين عائشةُ رضي الله عنها أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما أُنزِل عليه: {إذا جاء نصر الله والفتح} تَأَوَّلَ القرآنَ وبَادَرَ إلى امتثال أَمْرِ الله تعالى في قوله: {فسبح بحمد ربك واستغفره}، فكان يكثر أن يقول في حال ركوعه وسجوده أثناء الصلاة: «سبحانك» وتنزيهًا لك من كلِّ نقص عما لا يليق بك، «اللهم ربنا وبحمدك» بالثناء المحمود عليك لكمال ذاتك وصفاتك وأفعالك، «اللهم اغفر لي» وامْحُ عني ذنبي وتجاوز عنه.
hints_ar: استحباب الإكثار من هذا الدعاء في الركوع والسجود.
الاستغفار في آخر العُمْر فيه تَنبيهٌ أنْ تَخْتِمَ العبادات كذلك -وخصوصًا الصلاة- بالاستغفار، ليتدارك ما حصل فيها من النقص.
أحسن ما يُتَوَسَّل به إلى الله في قبول الدعاء هو ذِكْرُ مَحامده وتسبيحه وتنزيهه عن النقائص والعيوب.
فضيلة الاستغفار، وطلبه في كل حال.
كمال عبودية النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وامتثاله لأمر الله.
